CySA+ CS0-003 — max questions and duration?
column2: Maximum 85 questions (MCQ + PBQ) in 165 minutes.

#separator:: CySA+ passing score and scale?
column2: 750 on a scaled 100–900 scale.

#separator:: CySA+ four domain weights (D1..D4)?
column2: CS0-003: Security Operations 33% / Vulnerability Management 30% / Incident Response 20% / Reporting & Communication 17%. (Successor CS0-004 re-weights them 34 / 26 / 24 / 16.)

#separator:: CySA+ recommended (not required) experience?
column2: CS0-003: Network+, Security+, or equivalent knowledge, with a minimum of 4 years as an incident response analyst, SOC analyst, or equivalent.

#separator:: CySA+ CS0-003 English exam retirement date, and its successor?
column2: English exam retires 2026-12-22 (translations 2027-03-23); successor CS0-004 launched 2026-06-23.

#separator:: Why does log time synchronization (NTP) matter to an analyst?
column2: Hosts must share a clock so events across sources can be correlated into one timeline.

#separator:: Log normalization does what?
column2: Maps many log formats to common fields so one query spans firewalls, hosts and apps.

#separator:: Two things network segmentation gives an analyst?
column2: It limits blast radius and creates chokepoints where traffic can be monitored.

#separator:: What does Zero Trust mean for the analyst's telemetry?
column2: More identity-anchored telemetry and clearer policy-enforcement points to monitor.

#separator:: Three families of malicious-activity indicators in CySA+?
column2: Network-related, host-related, application-related.

#separator:: Beaconing indicates what?
column2: Regular periodic callbacks to a host — classic command-and-control (C2).

#separator:: A document app spawning a shell is what kind of indicator?
column2: Host-related: a suspicious parent-child process chain — likely code execution.

#separator:: Abnormal host resource consumption suggests what?
column2: Cryptomining, ransomware encryption or a runaway implant.

#separator:: Unexpected application output or errors suggest what?
column2: Injection attempts (SQL, command), fuzzing or exploitation (application-related indicator).

#separator:: Which tool confirms C2 or exfiltration in raw traffic?
column2: Packet capture (tcpdump, Wireshark).

#separator:: Which tool gives deep host visibility — processes, files, memory, response actions?
column2: Endpoint detection and response (EDR).

#separator:: Which tools investigate a domain or IP's age, owner and reputation?
column2: DNS lookups (nslookup/dig), whois and threat-intel reputation lookups.

#separator:: Sandboxing is for what?
column2: Detonating a suspect sample in isolation to observe its behavior safely.

#separator:: SIEM vs SOAR vs EDR in one line?
column2: SIEM correlates and alerts; SOAR automates playbooks; EDR gives host depth.

#separator:: Three levels of cyber threat intelligence?
column2: Strategic (leadership trends), operational (campaigns/intent), tactical (specific TTPs and IoCs the SOC can action).

#separator:: What is an ISAC?
column2: An Information Sharing and Analysis Center — a sector-specific community sharing threat data among members.

#separator:: IoC vs IoA?
column2: IoC = artifact evidence an intrusion occurred (hash/IP/domain); IoA = behavior showing an attack in progress — harder to evade.

#separator:: What is MITRE ATT&CK?
column2: A knowledge base of real-world adversary tactics and techniques used to map detection coverage and describe intrusions.

#separator:: Threat hunting is driven by what?
column2: A hypothesis (often from CTI or an ATT&CK technique) tested against the data — proactive search for what detection missed.

#separator:: What should every threat hunt produce?
column2: A new automated detection so the same threat is caught next time.

#separator:: Standardizing SOC processes uses which artifacts?
column2: Playbooks and runbooks so any analyst handles an alert the same way.

#separator:: Single pane of glass?
column2: One consolidated console so analysts are not switching between many tools.

#separator:: What should be automated in a SOC and what should stay human?
column2: Automate repetitive deterministic steps (enrichment, known-bad blocking, tickets); keep scoping, analysis and decisions human.

#separator:: Credentialed vs uncredentialed scan?
column2: Credentialed logs in and reads patch/config from inside — more accurate, fewer false positives; uncredentialed mimics an outsider's view.

#separator:: Internal vs external scan vantage?
column2: Internal shows the post-breach/insider view and lateral paths; external shows the attack surface an outsider can reach.

#separator:: Active vs passive scanning?
column2: Active sends probes (thorough but can disrupt); passive observes existing traffic (zero impact — ideal for OT).

#separator:: Safe approach to scanning fragile OT/ICS/SCADA systems?
column2: Prefer passive discovery and read-only checks; active scans only in maintenance windows, throttled, with owners present.

#separator:: False positive vs false negative?
column2: False positive = reported but not real (noise); false negative = real flaw the tool missed (the dangerous one).

#separator:: How are false negatives mitigated?
column2: Multiple tools, credentialed scans and manual testing.

#separator:: How does an analyst reconcile results from two scanners?
column2: Correlate by CVE/asset, remove duplicates, and reason why they differ (credentialed vs not, plug-in coverage, timing).

#separator:: CVSS three metric groups and who sets each?
column2: Base (intrinsic, set by publisher), Temporal/Threat (changes over time), Environmental (set by you for your organization).

#separator:: CVSS v3.x severity bands?
Does CVSS measure risk?
column2: No — it measures severity; risk = severity × exposure × asset value × likelihood of exploitation.

#separator:: EPSS is what?
column2: Exploit Prediction Scoring System (FIRST): a 0–1 probability a CVE is exploited in the wild within 30 days.

#separator:: CISA KEV is what?
column2: The Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog — CVEs confirmed exploited in the wild; membership pushes a finding to the top.

#separator:: CVSS vs EPSS vs KEV in one line?
column2: CVSS = how severe; EPSS = how likely; KEV = exploited now.

#separator:: Context factors beyond the score when prioritizing?
column2: Exploitability/weaponization, asset value, zero-day status, internal vs external exposure, organizational/industry impact.

#separator:: Four control categories in CySA+?
column2: Managerial (policy), operational (people/process), technical (technology), physical (locks/badges).

#separator:: What do you do when you cannot patch?
column2: Apply a compensating control — segmentation/isolation, tighter firewall rules, more monitoring, virtual patching via IPS/WAF.

#separator:: Risk acceptance — who signs and what is recorded?
column2: The risk owner formally signs off; the decision is documented, time-bounded and revisited.

#separator:: CVE vs CWE?
column2: CVE = a specific instance of a vulnerability in a product; CWE = the weakness class/root cause (e.g. CWE-89 SQLi).

#separator:: Cyber Kill Chain vs MITRE ATT&CK vs Diamond Model — shape?
column2: Kill Chain = linear 7 stages; ATT&CK = non-linear matrix of tactics × techniques; Diamond = four vertices.

#separator:: Four vertices of the Diamond Model?
column2: Adversary, capability, infrastructure, victim.

#separator:: Seven stages of the Cyber Kill Chain in order?
column2: Reconnaissance → Weaponization → Delivery → Exploitation → Installation → Command & Control → Actions on Objectives.

#separator:: ATT&CK tactic vs technique?
column2: Tactic = the adversary's goal (the why, e.g. Persistence); technique = the method (the how, a T#### ID).

#separator:: Four phases of the NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 IR life cycle?
column2: Preparation → Detection & Analysis → Containment, Eradication & Recovery (one phase) → Post-Incident Activity.

#separator:: What belongs to the Preparation phase?
column2: IR plan and playbooks, a CSIRT, a communication plan, tooling, training, tabletop exercises, hardening.

#separator:: What does the analyst do in Detection & Analysis?
column2: Validate the alert, triage/classify, determine scope/impact/severity, document a timeline, preserve evidence.

#separator:: Short-term vs long-term containment?
column2: Short-term isolates (pull cable, disable account) to buy time; long-term applies temporary fixes so business continues until eradication.

#separator:: Eradication means what?
column2: Remove the root cause: delete malware, close the exploited vulnerability, disable compromised accounts, rebuild from known-good images.

#separator:: Which comes first: containment or eradication?
column2: Containment — never wipe a box before containing spread and preserving evidence.

#separator:: What happens in Post-Incident Activity?
column2: Blameless lessons-learned meeting, root-cause analysis, IoC generation, reporting, updating plan/playbooks/controls.

#separator:: Order of volatility?
column2: CPU registers/cache → RAM → network state → running processes → disk → logs/archives → physical media.

#separator:: How is evidence acquired defensibly?
column2: Maintain chain of custody, follow order of volatility, hash to prove integrity, work on copies.

#separator:: Three factors for incident severity?
column2: Functional impact, information impact, recoverability.

#separator:: Three durable outputs of a well-managed incident?
column2: A timeline, a set of IoCs, and a root cause.

#separator:: Compliance report vs action plan?
column2: Compliance report demonstrates adherence to a standard/regulation; action plan assigns remediation steps, owners and dates.

#separator:: Vulnerability-program metrics to track?
column2: MTTR/MTTD, recurrence/reopen rate, scan coverage, SLA compliance, open criticals/highs over time.

#separator:: Inhibitors to remediation CompTIA names?
column2: MOU, SLA, organizational governance, business-process interruption, degrading functionality, legacy systems, proprietary systems.

#separator:: Why do legacy and proprietary systems inhibit remediation?
column2: Legacy may have no patch available; proprietary/vendor-locked systems cannot be modified by the customer.

#separator:: When remediation is blocked, what does the analyst recommend?
column2: A compensating control or documented risk acceptance — and reports residual risk to the risk owner.

#separator:: Due diligence vs disclosure (vuln management)?
column2: Due diligence = documented reasonable work to find/address risk; disclosure = reporting vulnerabilities internally, to vendors, or to customers/regulators as required.

#separator:: Incident declaration does what?
column2: Formally classifies an event as an incident — starting the response clock and notification obligations.

#separator:: Escalation follows what?
column2: A predefined path based on severity to the right responders and decision-makers.

#separator:: Who reviews external incident messaging first?
column2: Legal and public relations.

#separator:: Which external notifications are often legally mandated and time-bound?
column2: Regulator and customer/affected-individual notifications (e.g. GDPR 72-hour rule — verify).

#separator:: How should analysts communicate with non-technical stakeholders?
column2: Translate technical detail into risk and impact: business risk for leadership, plain-language facts for customers.

#separator:: Incident metrics for leadership?
column2: MTTD, mean time to respond/contain, mean time to recover, number of incidents, dwell time.
